questions: Should the function count letters from the dictionary keys (words) or from the dictionary values (letters)?
If two letters have the same frequency, how should they be sorted within that tie (e.g., alphabetically, arbitrary, by first appearance)?
Are the letters in the keys guaranteed to be lowercase alphabetic, or could they include uppercase, digits, or special characters?
Should the output dictionary include only letters that appear in the keys, or also include the values (single letters) as part of the count?
If a word in the keys contains repeated letters (e.g., 'apple' has two 'p's), should each occurrence be counted separately?
Is the input dictionary guaranteed to be non-empty, or should the function handle an empty dictionary?
Should the function treat the dictionary values (single letters) as irrelevant to the counting, or are they part of the data to be processed?
Are the words in the keys guaranteed to be strings, or could they be other iterable types?
